name: CS101 - Professional Programming Practices
description: Best practices for writing clean, maintainable code and problem-solving strategies

lessons.title: Week 4: Professional Coding Practices
lessons.description: Code quality, documentation, debugging, and testing

lessons.title: Week 5: From Ideas to Instructions
lessons.description: Planning, pseudocode, implementation workflow, and testing

questions.question: What makes a good variable name?
questions.answer: Descriptive, tells what it represents, uses meaningful words not abbreviations (e.g., 'total_price' not 'tp')
questions.explanation: Good names make code self-documenting and easier to understand

questions.question: What should a docstring explain?
choices: Why the function exists and what it accomplishes (the why)
questions.answer: Why the function exists and what it accomplishes (the why)
questions.explanation: Docstrings should explain purpose and intent, not just repeat the code

questions.question: When should you write comments?
questions.answer: When explaining WHY something is done a certain way, not WHAT the code does (the code shows what)
questions.explanation: Comments add context and rationale that isn't obvious from the code itself

questions.question: What is the benefit of 'keeping it clean' in code?
questions.answer: Makes debugging and maintenance easier
questions.explanation: Clean code is easier to read, understand, modify, and debug

questions.question: What makes code 'instantly readable'?
questions.answer: Consistent formatting, clear naming, logical organization, appropriate whitespace and indentation
questions.explanation: Readable code follows conventions and uses visual structure to guide understanding

questions.question: Why break long scripts into functions?
choices: To enable reuse, testing, and understanding of individual pieces
questions.answer: To enable reuse, testing, and understanding of individual pieces
questions.explanation: Functions promote modularity, reusability, and easier testing

questions.question: What is print tracing?
questions.answer: Adding strategic print statements to show variable values and program flow during execution
questions.explanation: Print tracing helps visualize what's happening inside your program

questions.question: What is an invariant?
questions.answer: A condition that should always be true at a certain point in the code; used as safety checkpoints
questions.explanation: Invariants help catch bugs by asserting expected conditions

questions.question: What makes a function reusable?
choices: No side effects, clear inputs/outputs, single responsibility
questions.answer: No side effects, clear inputs/outputs, single responsibility
questions.explanation: Reusable functions are self-contained and don't depend on external state

questions.question: What does 'stress it to the edge' mean in testing?
questions.answer: Test with extreme values: empty inputs, very large numbers, boundary cases, edge conditions
questions.explanation: Edge case testing reveals bugs that might not appear with normal inputs

questions.question: Why validate inputs before processing?
choices: To prevent crashes and ensure data quality
questions.answer: To prevent crashes and ensure data quality
questions.explanation: Input validation catches bad data before it causes problems

questions.question: What is refactoring?
questions.answer: Improving code structure without changing its external behavior
questions.explanation: Refactoring makes code cleaner and more maintainable while keeping functionality the same

questions.question: How do you ensure 'nothing breaks' during refactoring?
questions.answer: Run tests before and after changes to verify behavior stays the same
questions.explanation: Tests act as a safety net when modifying code

questions.question: What's the key to balancing planning and coding?
choices: Plan enough to start, then iterate
questions.answer: Plan enough to start, then iterate
questions.explanation: Over-planning wastes time; under-planning leads to confusion. Find the balance.

questions.question: What is the purpose of hierarchy in pseudocode?
questions.answer: To show the structure and relationships between steps; major steps at top, details nested below
questions.explanation: Hierarchical pseudocode reveals the logical organization of the solution

questions.question: What are common solution patterns?
questions.answer: Counter, accumulator, search, filter, map, reduce, sentinel loop, validation loop
questions.explanation: Recognizing patterns helps you solve similar problems faster

questions.question: What is a function stub?
choices: A placeholder function with signature but minimal implementation
questions.answer: A placeholder function with signature but minimal implementation
questions.explanation: Stubs let you build the overall structure before implementing details

questions.question: What does 'building code incrementally' mean?
questions.answer: Write small pieces, test each piece, then add more; don't write everything at once
questions.explanation: Incremental development catches errors early and builds confidence

questions.question: What is a test table?
questions.answer: A table with columns for inputs, expected outputs, and actual outputs to systematically test code
questions.explanation: Test tables organize test cases and make it easy to verify correctness

questions.question: What is dry running?
choices: Manually tracing through code/pseudocode with test values
questions.answer: Manually tracing through code/pseudocode with test values
questions.explanation: Dry running helps you understand and verify logic before or without running code

questions.question: What is a feature brief?
questions.answer: A clear statement of what feature you're building and why, written for understanding not implementation
questions.explanation: Feature briefs clarify the goal before diving into technical details

questions.question: What's the difference between purpose and technical details?
choices: Purpose is what and why; technical details are how
questions.answer: Purpose is what and why; technical details are how
questions.explanation: Understanding purpose before implementation prevents solving the wrong problem

questions.question: What should a structured problem statement include?
questions.answer: Clear goal, constraints, assumptions, inputs, outputs, and success criteria
questions.explanation: Complete problem statements prevent misunderstandings and scope creep

questions.question: Why define example inputs and outputs?
choices: To clarify expectations and create test cases
questions.answer: To clarify expectations and create test cases
questions.explanation: Examples make abstract requirements concrete and testable

questions.question: How do you break down into subproblems?
questions.answer: Identify independent pieces that can be solved separately, each with clear inputs/outputs
questions.explanation: Breaking problems into subproblems makes complex tasks manageable

questions.question: Why sequence subproblems logically?
questions.answer: Some subproblems depend on others; solving in correct order prevents rework
questions.explanation: Dependency order matters: validate before processing, process before displaying

questions.question: What does 'prioritizing tasks by risk' mean?
choices: Do uncertain/difficult tasks first to learn early
questions.answer: Do uncertain/difficult tasks first to learn early
questions.explanation: Tackling risky tasks early prevents late surprises and wasted work

questions.question: What is a function pipeline?
questions.answer: Connecting functions where the output of one becomes the input of the next
questions.explanation: Pipelines break complex processing into clear, testable stages
